x: Our other men to finish, with nine to compete and six to score, were Les Stokell 64th, Albert Frost 95th, and finally Dick Tobin 132nd. It is interesting to note that Denis Brickwood finished in 80th place, and was then running for Mitcham A.C., and it is perhaps sad to reflect that of our team memb…

The Southern Champs the following month at Eastbourne at which the Club usually made a strong showing resulted in another 4th place behind T.V.H., Aylesford and Blackheath, our first man home being Les Stokell with a good performance by evergreen Ted Stimpson in 21st place.

Our positions were as follows:- 3 V.S.Blowfield 56:46; 4 E.S.Stimpson 57:24; 7 L.W.Herbert 57:50; 10 F.J.Abberton 58:05; 15 T.P.Clinton 58:20; 36 C.T.Carter 60:01; 38 C.L.Stokell 60:05; 65 R.W.Tobin 61:37; 84 S.R.Eales 62:25; 90 A.E.Frost 62:50; 106 A.F.Mitchell 63:28; 132 G.M.Pearson 64:15.
The Seniors, led home by Les Stokell were 8th; the Juniors with Charlie Walker in 40th place were 21st and the Youths with Don Maclean in 18th place were 7th.
Les Stokell passed away at Sidmouth in Devon on 20 January 2001 in his 82nd year. He was an active club member in the early post-war years, having joined the Club at the age of 27 in 1946.
